title: The blender valuable and its bill soup
summary: One of R.E.P.O.'s trap valuables is a blender: it keeps a timer of its own, blades with start, loop and end sounds and loops for being stuck and empty, a lid that pops, and money inside it that becomes a bill soup.
body: This one is a machine before it is a prize. It is a trap first: the game keeps whether the trap has been triggered, whether it is active, whether it has started, whether it works on a timer, and the rarity level it activates at.
It runs on a timer of its own, so the blender is something that starts and then does its work rather than reacting the instant it is touched.
Its blades are modelled in detail. There is a blade and a speed for it, a curve for how it moves, and a transform for the machine's mesh, so the jug and what is inside it can be animated together.

It sounds like a blender being pushed too far. There are separate sounds for the blades starting, running and stopping, and loops of their own for the blades being stuck and for an empty jug, which is how the machine tells you it is struggling.
It is also where the money goes. There is money in it, a second money part, and a bill soup with a curve of its own, so what is being blended is modelled rather than only being described.
The lid comes off. Its cap pops, with a collider of its own, and there are particles for the bills, for bills thrown at random, for dust and for the cap, so the moment of opening is drawn in parts.
It blasts as well, with a centre of its own that the blast comes from, which is how the machine can hurt what is standing next to it.
It carries a hurt collider of its own, so what it damages is a decided area rather than everything nearby.
It knows whether it is the copy that matters locally, and monsters can be set to come and investigate it, so the noise of a running blender is a way to bring something to you.
The image beside this entry is the game's own: the colour sheet it ships for the blender's body, with the buttons, the dial and the jug all on one sheet.
What this entry does not tell you: how long the timer is, how much the blender is worth, or what the bill soup is for. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: It keeps whether the trap is triggered, active or started, whether it triggers on a timer, and the rarity at which it activates.
facts.evidence: identifiers: trapTriggered, trapActive, trapStart, triggerOnTimer, trapActivateRarityLevel

facts.claim: It has a timer of its own.
Its blades have a speed, a curve and the machine a mesh transform of its own.
There are separate sounds for the blades starting, looping and ending, plus a loop for being stuck and one for an empty jug.
facts.evidence: identifiers: soundBladeStart, soundBladeLoop, soundBladeEnd, soundBladeStuckLoop, soundBladeEmptyLoop

facts.claim: There is money in it, a second money part, and a bill soup with a curve of its own.
Its cap pops and has a collider, with particles for the bills, random bills, dust and the cap.
facts.evidence: identifiers: capPop, cap, capCollider, billParticles, billParticlesRandom, dustParticles, capParticle

facts.claim: It blasts from a centre of its own.
It has a hurt collider of its own.
It keeps track of whether it is the local copy, and monsters can be made to investigate it.
